llm.summary: The skill is mostly a disclosed model router, but its privacy mode can select a cloud-configured primary model and it can store message snippets locally without clear safeguards.

dimensions.detail: The code reads local Ollama config files, uses a built-in cloud model catalog, and creates a ~/.model-router directory, which generally fits the model-routing purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The quick-start command uses npx clawhub@latest, a mutable installer reference. No artifact evidence shows the reviewed package fetches or executes remote payloads itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The activation instructions are broad, including sensitive-data mentions, complex-task keywords, and configuration requests; this is related to routing but can affect prompts users may not expect to route automatically.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Context tracking can persist the first 200 characters of messages to ~/.model-router/contexts.json in plaintext without explicit permissions, retention controls, redaction, or clear opt-in disclosure.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is coherent, but the artifact claims sensitive data is forced local while router.py only selects the configured primary model and does not enforce that it is local.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use this only if you are comfortable with automatic routing decisions, verify that primary_model in ~/.model-router/models.json is truly local before entering secrets, and treat context tracking as local plaintext storage of message snippets. Prefer a pinned installer version and avoid running the install command with elevated privileges.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: Broad routing triggers are consistent with an automatic router, but sensitive-data activation should be made more explicit to users.
[RP1] unexpected: The unpinned npx @latest installer is a supply-chain caution, not evidence that this artifact is malicious.
[RA2] expected: The cited ~/.model-router path is an optional configuration/state location, not a cron job, startup hook, or backdoor-style persistence.
[SQP-2] expected: Context persistence is advertised, but storing raw message snippets in plaintext is under-disclosed and supports Review.
[SQP-3] expected: Automatic privacy routing is disclosed and privacy-oriented; the material concern is that the implementation does not enforce local-only routing.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The detector docstring overstates environment-variable detection and availability checks; this is documentation drift, not a standalone security issue.
[T09] expected: The plaintext context-storage warning is supported by context.py and is a material local confidentiality concern.
[T09] unexpected: The privacy-routing warning is supported: a cloud model can be configured as primary and returned for sensitive prompts despite local-only claims.
[T08] unexpected: The unpinned installation command is a real caution but does not by itself establish malicious behavior in the reviewed skill.
